text:
maria_platform: Heads up — I'm putting a short proposal in the RFC bucket for how we handle token TTLs and attribution when one project/service account impersonates another across org boundaries. quick summary below, please react/comment.

maria_platform: Problem: when proj-A issues an impersonation request to SA in proj-B we currently lose clear attribution (who gets billed, who owns quota, and what shows up in the console). Also TTL semantics are inconsistent across SDKs.

maria_platform: Proposal (high level): 1) add an optional origin_affinity flag on the token-exchange endpoint (enum: inherit|isolate|foreign) 2) return explicit auth_chain in token response and telemetry 3) token TTL = min(requested_ttl, parent_token_ttl, sa_max_ttl). default preserves legacy behavior for 2 weeks.

maria_platform: Example response snippet:```json
{
  "access_token": "ya29...",
  "expires_at": "2026-05-03T15:24:00Z",
  "auth_chain": ["org:acme","proj:payments","sa:billing-runner"],
  "origin_affinity": "inherit"
}
```

amy_dev: :thinking_face: quick Q — will adding auth_chain bloat telemetry? can we limit to 3 entries max?

dylan_infra: I think we need auth_chain for routing and quota. If we charge the wrong project we open a billing/abuse vector. We should charge the effective resource owner by default (where SA lives) unless origin_affinity == "inherit".

kevin_security: Security: must avoid PII in any metric. auth_chain should use stable opaque IDs (org_id, proj_id, sa_id hashed) not human email. Also TTL rule is sane — explicit expires_at is a hard requirement for audits.

sofia_pm: UX: Console should show an "Acting as" chip with the chain and a hover that links to audit logs and quota breakdown. Add a toggle in project billing to choose whether cross-project impersonation accrues to caller or callee (billing admin opt-in).

amy_dev: Implementation note: current token-exchange clients assume the response shape. We should introduce /v2/token-exchange and keep /v1 behavior, or add an opt-in query param. v2 returns auth_chain + expires_at.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: feature-flag=auth-chain-v0 enabled for infra-canary us-east-1 at 05:30 UTC

dylan_infra: telemetry proposal: metric tags: auth_chain_hash (list up to 3), origin_affinity, effective_owner_id, billed_owner_id. For dashboards, show a drop-down to filter by effective_owner.

kevin_security: Also: redact/hide auth_chain in high-cardinality logs. expose only in traced spans tied to request id, not in bulk metrics.

maria_platform: OK — next steps: I'll draft RFC with API schema + migration timeline. Suggest default: preserve legacy (no auth_chain) for 14 days, then v2 enforced and console shows 'acting-as' chain. @sofia_pm can you own the console mocks and the billing opt-in wording?

sofia_pm: Yep — I'll add mocks and a rollout checklist (billing docs, support playbook, e2e tests).

maria_platform: Thanks — dropping the RFC link in here shortly.
